sn1.2:1.1: From here, the Pali gives only the abbreviated setting or none at all. In such cases, we are meant to read the full introduction per [sn1.1]().
sn1.2:5.1: The Buddha’s answer seems to mix a few lines of verse with some prose. This line is verse, as it has an unusual structure, best understood as due to the exigencies of metre, and where it occurs elsewhere it is always as verse. Only this line and the next are metrical. The Chinese parallels at SA 1268 and SA-2 179 format the whole of the Buddha’s answer as prose, the verse being spoken by the deity at the end. Nonetheless, it does seem as if these first two lines correspond with SA 1268’s 愛喜滅盡，我心 解脫.
sn1.2:5.2: With this the Buddha differentiates himself from Yājnavalkya, for whom perception (limited awareness) ends, but consciousness (infinite awareness) is eternal (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 2.4.12).
